ahi.etymon_note: POLLEX AFI.1 PPN *afi "fire"; Wiktionary agrees. Words kahuahi, kiaahi, lehuahi, ʻōʻōahi.

aho#1.etymon_note: POLLEX AHO PCE *aho "breath", a set apart from AFO PPN *afo "cord" (aho#0, unused). Words aholoa, ahonui, pauaho.

ahu.etymon_note: POLLEX QAFU.2 PPN *qafu "heap up; a heap or raised place". Word ahupuaʻa (the boundary heap).
ahu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Altar, shrine, heap up, pile"; Wiktionary "heap, pile, mound; cairn"

akamai.etymon_note: POLLEX QATAMAI.A PPN *qatamai "intelligent, expert, clever". Word akeakamai. Tahitian atama omitted (POLLEX flags it irregular).
akamai.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Clever, expert"; Wiktionary "intelligent, smart, clever"

ake.etymon_note: POLLEX QATE.1 PPN *qate "liver" (seat of feeling; Māori takuate "yearn" is in the same set); Wiktionary has one etymology for both senses. One etymon, kept as one stone per DECISIONS B9. akeloa and akemāmā use liver (POLLEX *qate-loa "spleen"), akeakamai uses desire.
ake.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Liver"; Wiktionary "liver; to yearn for, desire"

akua.etymon_note: POLLEX QATUA PPN *qatua "deity, spirit". The PEP *atua row (Akua, a night of the moon) is a different homograph and is not attached. Word kahuakua.
akua.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Deity"; Wiktionary "god; any supernatural being, spirit"

ala#0.etymon_note: POLLEX HALA PPN *hala "road, path"; POLLEX also has alanui < PCE *ara-nui and alahaka < PCE *ara-fata. Words alahaka, alahao, alakaʻi, alaloa, alanui, alawai, alaʻula.

ala#1.etymon_note: POLLEX QARA PPN *qara "awake"; the only word, makaʻala, is POLLEX MATA-QARA PPN *mata-qara, which P&E spells with ʻokina, so the stone reads ʻALA (DECISIONS B10). Id kept as ala#1.
ala#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) ala "Awake"; makaʻala "Alert, vigilant, watchful, awake"

alakaʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX HALA-TAKI PPN *hala-taki "to lead", an inherited compound used here as one stone (DECISIONS B6). Word kumualakaʻi.
alakaʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Lead, guide, direct"; Wiktionary "to lead, to guide"

aliʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX QARIKI PPN *qariki "chief". Words aliʻiwahine, halealiʻi, leialiʻi, moʻoaliʻi, nohoaliʻi, pāpalealiʻi.
aliʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Chief"; Wiktionary "a hereditary rank of traditional chief"

alo.etymon_note: POLLEX QARO.A PPN *qaro "front, face". Word ʻaialo (those who eat in the chief’s presence).
alo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Front, face, presence"; Wiktionary "front; face; presence"

aloha.etymon_note: POLLEX QAROFA.A PPN *qarofa "love, pity, compassion" (QAROFA.B "greeting" is a sub-sense of the same set). Word hoaaloha.

ana#1.etymon_note: POLLEX HAGA.1 PPN *haŋa "span (measurement)", not QANA.1 *qana "cave" (ana#0, unused). Words anamanaʻo, anapuni, anawaena, anaʻāina.
ana#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Measure"; Wiktionary "measurement; to measure, survey"

ani.etymon_note: POLLEX AGI.1 PPN *aŋi "blow (of wind, breeze)". Word anilā.
ani.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Blow (of wind, breeze)"; Wiktionary "to blow softly (as a breeze)"

aniani#0.etymon_note: POLLEX QALI.1A PPN *qali "clearly visible, transparent": P&E aniani as a variant of aliali "crystal clear" (POLLEX flags the n as phonologically irregular). Not AGI.2 aniani "travel swiftly". Word makaaniani.
aniani#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Mirror, glass; clear, transparent, obvious"

ao#0.etymon_note: POLLEX QAHO PPN *qaho "day (not night)", a set apart from QAO.1 *qao "cloud". Words naʻauao, ʻōpūao (light as enlightenment).
ao#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Day (not night)"; Wiktionary "light; daylight; day"

ao#2.etymon_note: POLLEX QAO.1 PPN *qao "cloud". Words aouli, kiaao, nānāao.

ao?ʻahuao.etymon_note: Unresolved. Not day or cloud; the only source is Andrews. POLLEX has P&E ʻao "new shoot, sprout" < PEP *kao, so the word may be ʻahuʻao with a different stone; P&E must settle. Word ʻahuao.
ao?ʻahuao.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "ao, the young leaves of the lauhala tree" (placeholder until checked)

au.etymon_note: POLLEX QAU.1 PPN *qau "current". Words aumiki, kaiau, lanaau. aumoe split off (POLLEX *aqu-mohe).

au?aumoe.etymon_note: Unresolved, split from au (current). POLLEX AQU-MOHE (P&E aumoe) and Wiktionary derive aumoe from *aqu-mohe; Andrews and Johnson 2008 read au "time". Not *qau, so it must not link to the current stone. Word aumoe.
au?aumoe.gloss_source: POLLEX note to PN *aqu-mohe "fast asleep" (Cf. PPN *aqu "come, reach, arrive"); Wiktionary etymology of aumoe

aʻa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX AKA.A PPN *aka "root". Words aʻakoko, aʻalele, aʻalolo, paʻiaʻa (POLLEX PNP *paki-aka "root system").
aʻa#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Small root"; Wiktionary "root; vein; blood vessel; sinew (nerve)"

aʻo.etymon_note: POLLEX AKO PPN *ako "learn, teach". Word ʻōleloaʻo.

ea.etymon_note: POLLEX EQA.A PPN *eqa "come to the surface; come up for air". kaiea uses rise, kinoea air, waiea breath/life. The sovereignty sense (EQA.B) is a sub-set of the same entry; no word here uses it.
ea.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Rise, go up; life, breath, spirit"; Wiktionary "air, breath; gas, vapor; to rise"

emi.etymon_note: No POLLEX row for Hawaiian emi; Wiktionary gives PPN *qemi "flinch, draw back", not used without POLLEX. Word kūemi.
emi.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 emi v. "to fall behind… to recede"; Wiktionary "to diminish" (etymon *qemi "flinch, draw back")

eʻe.etymon_note: POLLEX HEKE PPN *heke "to mount, go on board, perch". Word kaieʻe (the sea that climbs onto land).
eʻe.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Mount"; Wiktionary "to get on, to board; to climb on"

hai#0.etymon_note: POLLEX FAQI PNP *faqi "rite, perform ritual". Word haipule. Other cognates omitted: POLLEX marks the Sāmoan and Tongan ones problematic.

haka#0.etymon_note: POLLEX FATA.1 PPN *fata "shelf, platform", not FATA.2 PNP *fata "gap". Words hakakau and alahaka (POLLEX PCE *ara-fata "bridge or ladder", cf. *fata "shelf").
haka#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Shelf"; Wiktionary "shelf, rack; perch, roost; platform"

haka?hakamoa.etymon_note: Unresolved. Andrews reads haka "to quarrel" (cf. hakakā), but haka "roost" (haka#0) fits too, and no source settles it. Word hakamoa.
haka?hakamoa.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "haka, to quarrel" (placeholder until checked)

hakahaka.etymon_note: POLLEX FATA.2 PNP *fata "gape, gap" (reduplicated). Word makahakahaka.
hakahaka.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Vacant space, vacancy, room; blanks, gap"

haku#0.etymon_note: POLLEX FATU.4 PCE *fatu "chief", apart from *fatu "stone" and *fatu "weave; compose". Words hakuhale, hakuwahine, hakuʻāina.
haku#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui 1986) "Lord, master, overseer"; Wiktionary "lord, master, owner"

haku#2.etymon_note: POLLEX FATU.1B PPN *fatu "compose, construct" (FATU.1A "braid, plait" is the same set). Words hakumele, hakuʻōlelo.
haku#2.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Compose, invent"; Wiktionary "to compose, to arrange"

hala#0.etymon_note: POLLEX SALA.1 PPN *sala "err, error". Words kalahala, lawehala.
hala#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Err, error; to pass by, to miss"; Wiktionary "sin; error"

hala#1.etymon_note: POLLEX FARA PPN *fara "pandanus"; lau hala is PNP *lau-fala. Words lauhala, leihala.

hale.etymon_note: POLLEX FALE PPN *fale "house". 19 words (hale pule, hale aliʻi, kahua hale…).

hamo.etymon_note: No POLLEX set for hamo "rub on"; the POLLEX hamo row (PCE *samo, a sweet-potato variety) is another homograph and is not attached. Word hamoʻula.
hamo.gloss_source: Wiktionary "to rub (on); to besmear, to spread"; Andrews–Parker 1922 "to rub over; to besmear"

hana#0.etymon_note: POLLEX SAGA.1A PPN *saŋa "work, make, do" (Wiktionary says PNP; POLLEX level used). Not hana "warm" (*fana). Nine words.
hana#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Work, labour"; Wiktionary "work; to work, do, make"

hanauna.etymon_note: POLLEX FANAU-GA PNP *fanau-ŋa "a kin group", a derived word used as one stone (DECISIONS B6). Word hoahanauna.

hanu.etymon_note: POLLEX FAGU.2 PPN *faŋu "breathe, blow through the nose" (Sāmoan fagufagu is the nose flute). Word hanupaʻa.
hanu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Breathe, smell, sniff"; Wiktionary "breath; to breathe"

hao#0.etymon_note: POLLEX FAQO.1A PPN *faqo "peg, wooden nail", not FAQAO *faqao "seize, rob". Nine words; paʻahao kept here ("stuck in irons", Andrews; Hale Paʻahao) though Wiktionary reads hao "robber".
hao#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Iron, bit; horn"; Wiktionary "iron; metal tools"

hau#0.etymon_note: POLLEX SAU.1 PPN *sau "dew" (not SAU.6 "breeze", not FAU.A "hibiscus"). Words hauʻeli (frost) and haupia (Wiktionary only: hau "ice, dew").
hau#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Dew"; Wiktionary "dew; ice, snow, frost; cool"

hau#mood.etymon_note: POLLEX SAU.7 PPN *sau "(in compounds) temperament", with P&E hau/ʻoli; Wiktionary agrees. Word hauʻoli. Its other reflexes are compounds only, so no cognates.
hau#mood.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) under PPN *sau "(in compounds) temperament, disposition"; Wiktionary hau "temperament, in compounds"

heihei.etymon_note: No POLLEX row; no ancestor given. Word heiheinalu.
heihei.gloss_source: Wiktionary "race; to race"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "heihei, to run"

hele.etymon_note: POLLEX SELE.4 PEC *sele "go". Sāmoan sele omitted (POLLEX marks it vulgar). Words helekū, hoahele, hōkūhele, kaʻahele, pōhakuhele.

helekū.etymon_note: A compound (hele + kū) used as one stone (DECISIONS B6); no POLLEX row. Word manuhelekū.

hema.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *sema 'left (not right)' (SEMA.1), one Wiktionary etymology; words kūkulu hema (the left-hand point, south), lima hema.

henehene.etymon_note: No POLLEX set. Wiktionary: reduplication of hene 'to snicker'; a reduplicated stem as one stone (B7 b), never linked to hene. Word ʻakahenehene.

hewa.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *sewa 'confused, in error' (SEWA.A); words kuhihewa, kūhewa, makehewa, moehewa, wahahewa all bracket hewa 'wrong'.
hewa.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'mistake, fault, error'; Wiktionary 'mistake; wrong'

heʻe#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *feke 'octopus' (FEKE); word kiloheʻe (looking for octopus).

heʻe#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *seke 'slip, slide; surf-ride' (SEKE.1A); words heʻe nalu (wave sliding), wahaheʻe (slippery mouth). Wiktionary's entry also holds heʻe 'flee', which POLLEX files apart (SEKE.2) and no word here uses. Family under A16.
heʻe#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'slip, slide; surf'; Wiktionary 'to slide, to surf, to slip'

hiamoe.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fia-mohe 'to be sleepy' (FIA-MOHE): an inherited compound kept as one stone (B6); never links to moe. Words kulihiamoe, makahiamoe.
hiamoe.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'sleep, to sleep; fall asleep'

hiki.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *fiti 'climb, rise, appear (esp. of heavenly bodies)' (FITI.1B; cf. lā hiki 'rising sun'); word hikimoe (the west, where the sun arrives to lie down).
hiki.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'arise, appear, reach a place, come'; Wiktionary 'to reach, arrive'

hiki?hikilele.etymon_note: Unresolved. POLLEX has the whole word as PCE *fiti-rere 'be startled' (Tahitian hitirere). Whether that *fiti is the root of hiki 'arrive, appear' (FITI.1B, hikimoe) is not stated, so it stays a stone of its own; no ancestor printed because only the compound is reconstructed.
hiki?hikilele.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) hikilele 'jump or start from shock'; PCE *fiti-rere 'be startled; start in surprise' (lele carries 'jump')

hina#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *sina 'grey or white-haired' (SINA.1), not *siŋa 'fall' (hina#1); word poʻohina (gray head).

hiʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *siki 'lift; carry or hold a child in the arms' (SIKI.1A), not the mat-edging *siki (SIKI.2); words hiʻilani, hiʻipoi (Andrews: hiʻi 'to lift up').
hiʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'carry in the arms'; Wiktionary 'to hold or carry in the arms'

hoa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *soa 'friend, partner, companion' (SOA), not *foa 'strike' (hoa#1); all thirteen hoa- words bracket hoa 'companion'.
hoa#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'friend'; Wiktionary 'friend, companion, associate, partner, peer'

hoe.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fohe 'paddle' (FOHE); words hoe uli, hoe waʻa, lauhoe.

hola#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fola 'spread out' (FOLA), not the fish-poison plant hola (PCE *sora); word papahola (Andrews: hola 'spread out').

holo#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *solo 'go quickly' (SOLO.3), not *solo 'landslide' (SOLO.1) or the food bundle (holo#bundle); words holokai, holo lio, holomoku.
holo#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'run; sail, ride, go'; Wiktionary 'to go, run; to sail, ride'

holo#bundle.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *solo 'food made with grated taro' (SOLO.2B; P&E 'a long bundle, as of hard poi'), a set apart from holo 'run' (SOLO.3); Andrews brackets holo ʻai the same way. POLLEX lists no cognate in the six card languages.
holo#bundle.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'a long bundle, as of hard poi'; Andrews–Parker bracket 'Holo, bundle'

holo?holowaʻa.etymon_note: Unresolved. No source says which holo makes a trough or chest (not 'run', not 'bundle' on any evidence); stays a stone of its own. Gloss left empty rather than guessed.
holo?holowaʻa.gloss_source: none: Andrews–Parker's bracket [Holo and waa, canoe] leaves holo unglossed

honua#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *fenua 'country, land' (FENUA); POLLEX marks the Hawaiian form phonologically irregular (o for e; Wiktionary: doublet of henua). Word mokuhonua (continent).

hope.etymon_note: POLLEX PEP *sope 'rear end' (SOPE.2); words hope poʻo (the head after), hoʻi hope (return backward), mulihope (last end).
hope.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'behind, after'; Wiktionary 'back, rear; last'

hou.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *foqou 'new' (FOQOU); Andrews brackets ʻōʻōhou as 'new digging tool'. Wiktionary's single hou entry also holds hou 'thrust, pierce' (PPN *fohu) and P&E has hou 'sweat' (PCE *hou): other etyma, not this stone.
hou.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'new, fresh, recent'; Andrews–Parker bracket 'hou, new'

hoʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *foki 'return' (FOKI.1), not the particle *foki 'also' (FOKI.2); word hoʻi hope (turn back).
hoʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'return'; Wiktionary 'to return (go or come back)'

hoʻoluʻu.etymon_note: A derived word (hoʻo- + luʻu 'dive, immerse', PPN *ruku) kept as one stone under B6 option 2, pending P&E's own hoʻoluʻu entry; POLLEX has no set for the derived form, so no ancestor is printed. Word waihoʻoluʻu (dyeing liquid).
hoʻoluʻu.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to plunge or dip something in liquids, dyes'

hua.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fua 'fruit; egg' (FUA.3A); words hua moa (egg of the fowl), huaʻai (fruit to eat). hua 'word, letter' is now hua#word (A2). The kumu ruling on this stone (A2) is still open; print only 'fruit, egg'.
hua.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'fruit' (PPN gloss 'fruit; to bear fruit; egg'); Wiktionary 'fruit; egg; seed'

hua#word.etymon_note: POLLEX files P&E's hua 'word, letter, figure' apart from *fua 'fruit' (under PPN *sua 'commence a chant', flagged Uncertain Semantic Connection, so no ancestor or cognates are printed). Split per A2; words hua mele (Andrews: hua 'letter'), huaʻōlelo.
hua#word.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'word, letter, figure'; Andrews–Parker bracket 'Hua, letter'

hue.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *fue 'calabash-gourd' (FUE.1B); words huewai, hue ʻili, ʻōpūhue all bracket hue 'gourd, calabash'.
hue.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'gourd, water calabash'; Wiktionary 'bottle gourd; calabash'

hui.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fuhi 'be in a group; gather' (FUHI.B; the 'bunch' sense FUHI.A is the same set); word huikala (Andrews: hui 'to join').
hui.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'join, unite, combine'; Wiktionary 'to meet; to unite, join'

huki.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *futi 'pull on a line or rope' (FUTI.1); word hukiwai (draw water).
huki.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'pull'; Wiktionary 'to pull, to tug'

huli#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fuli 'turn' (FULI.1), not *suli 'taro top' or huli#1 'seek'; words hulilua (turning two ways), hulipoepoe (turning sphere).
huli#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'turn (round or over)'; Wiktionary 'to turn; to reverse'

hulu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fulu 'body hair, feathers' (FULU.1), not *fulu 'nature, sort' (FULU.3) or *sulu 'cloth'; words huluʻiʻiwi (ʻiʻiwi feathers), kai hulu (Andrews: 'hairy' sea).
hulu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'hair, feather'; Wiktionary 'hair; fur; feather'

huna#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PEC *fuŋa 'crumb, grain, scrap' (FUGA.2), not *funa 'conceal' (A10); words hunakai (sea foam), lelehuna (flying particles).
huna#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'particle, grain, crumb, small'; Wiktionary 'particle, speck'

hā#2.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *faqa 'stalk' (FAQA.1), not hā 'four' (FAA.1) or hā 'breathe' (PEP *saa); words hāipu, hākō, hāniu all bracket hā 'stem of a leaf'.
hā#2.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'stalk'; Wiktionary 'stalk of a leaf'

hāliʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *faaliki 'cover floor with mats; floor covering' (FAALIKI); word hāliʻikuli (Andrews: hāliʻi 'to spread').
hāliʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) '(spread) covering'; Wiktionary 'to cover, to spread'

hānau.etymon_note: POLLEX set FAANAU: PPN *faanau 'offspring' (A) and PNP *faanau 'give birth; be born' (B), one etymon; words hoahānau, hānaukahi, hānau mua, one hānau use 'born'.
hānau.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'give birth; born'; Wiktionary 'birth; to give birth'

hōkū.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *fetuqu 'star' (FETUQU); words hōkū hele, hōkūlele, hōkūnaʻi, hōkū ʻaeʻa.

hū#0.etymon_note: No POLLEX set for hū 'rise, swell, overflow' (POLLEX's only Hawaiian hū is *fuu 'roar', hū#1). Andrews brackets hū 'ooze', 'rise', 'overflow' in hūkai, hūlani, hūpuna. Wiktionary's hū#0 also lumps hū 'stray', 'gum', 'commoners' and a variant of hui; this stone is only the rise/overflow sense.
hū#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to rise, swell; to surge, boil, flow, overflow'

ihu.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *isu 'nose' (ISU.1); words manu ihu (canoe beak-piece), pukaihu (nostril).
ihu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'nose'; Wiktionary 'nose; beak; prow of a boat'

inu.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *inu 'drink' (INU); word ʻahāinu (company for drinking).

ipu.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *ipu 'container for liquid' (IPU); word hāipu (gourd-leaf stalk) uses the gourd plant.
ipu.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'bottle gourd; vessel or container'

kaha#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tafa 'cut lengthwise, incise' (TAFA.2); words kahapili, kahapōʻai (Andrews: kaha 'a mark', 'in mathematics, a line').
kaha#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'cut open, scratch, mark, draw'; Wiktionary 'line, stripe; to mark'

kaha#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tafa 'side, edge' (TAFA.1A); kahakai is the inherited PNP *tafa-tai 'seashore' (Māori tahatai), which settles it; kahaone follows Wiktionary 'place'.

kaha?kahawai.etymon_note: Unresolved (adjudication and P18): Wiktionary reads kaha 'place' (kaha#1, as in kahakai), Andrews brackets kaha 'cut' with 'channel of a stream. See kahawai' (kaha#0); no POLLEX compound. Both candidates are PPN *tafa.
kaha?kahawai.gloss_source: none settled: Wiktionary kaha 'place'; Andrews–Parker bracket 'Kaha, cut'

kaha?kūkaha.etymon_note: Unresolved. 'Turn away' points to kaha#2 (soar, pass by; PPN *tafa, TAFA.3), 'stand sideways' to kaha#1 (side; TAFA.1A). Every candidate is PPN *tafa, so that ancestor could be printed once the sense is settled.
kaha?kūkaha.gloss_source: none settled: Andrews–Parker bracket 'kaha, to turn away'; Wiktionary kaha 'place' or 'to pass by'

kahi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *tasi 'one' (TASI.1), cf. PPN *tau-tasa for kaukahi itself; words hānaukahi, kaukahi, kiakahi, kiko kahi, kuʻikahi. P&E's free-standing form is kāhi; in compounds P&E writes kahi (kaukahi).

kahi#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tasi 'scrape, shave, whittle' (TASI.2), not *tasi 'one'; word koʻikahi (Andrews: kahi 'to cut or shave').
kahi#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'cut longitudinally'; Wiktionary 'to scrape; to shave, to plane'

kahiki#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *tafiti 'Tahiti' (TAFITI.1); words ʻuala kahiki, ʻulu kahiki (foreign sweet potato, breadfruit).
kahiki#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'any foreign country'; Wiktionary 'foreign country'

kahiko.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *tafito 'ancient, old' (TAFITO.B), Wiktionary's one etymology; word luna kahiko. Andrews' kahiko 'garments; to dress, adorn' is another word, not this stone.
kahiko.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'old, ancient; old person'; Wiktionary 'old, traditional'

kahu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX set TAFU, PPN *tafu 'light a fire': A 'tend oven', B (PEP) 'honored attendant, guardian', C (PMQ *tafu(-afi)) 'one who tends an oven', with Marquesan tahuahi 'servant who lights the fire'. Lettered sub-sets of one set are one root (B8, B9), so keeper and fire-tender are one stone and Wiktionary's kahu#1 (oven) merges here. Words kahu akua, kahu puaʻa, kahu wai, kahu ʻāina, kahu ahi.
kahu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'honored attendant, guardian, nurse' and 'one who tends an oven'; Wiktionary 'keeper, guardian, caretaker'

kahua.etymon_note: POLLEX PEP *tafuqa 'platform, foundation, base' (TAFUQA), Wiktionary's one etymology; word kahua hale. Andrews' kahua 'envy' and 'to designate' are other words.
kahua.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'foundation, base, site, location'; Wiktionary 'foundation; base; platform (of a house); site'

kai.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tahi 'shallow sea, salt water, tide' (TAHI.1), Wiktionary's one etymology; all 17 words use sea or salt water (holokai, kahakai, paʻakai, kai eʻe, waikai …). Andrews' kai 'to lead' is kaʻi, and his kai 'net, snare' is another word; neither is used.
kai.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'sea, seawater, area near the sea'; Wiktionary 'sea; seawater'

kaka?kakaʻōlelo.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart. The stone is spelled kākā to match the word kākāʻōlelo; that spelling rules out kaka 'rinse' (POLLEX TAA.1E, which P&E spells short). The likely root is kākā 'strike, fence' (Andrews kaka v. 'to beat; to strike'), which has no POLLEX row and no Wiktionary entry, so neither gloss nor ancestor is printed until P&E confirms.
kaka?kakaʻōlelo.gloss_source: none settled: Andrews' bracket [Kaka and olelo, word] leaves kaka unglossed; P&E's Lit. 'fencing [with] words' is known only second-hand

kala#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TALA.1, PPN *tala 'spine, prong' (P&E files the spined surgeonfish here); Wiktionary kala#0. Word puakala (Andrews: kala 'rough'; the prickly poppy). POLLEX's four *tala sets and *tara 'gable' are separate etyma.
kala#0.gloss_source: POLLEX PPN *tala 'sharp-pointed object, spine, prong' (P&E kala 'surgeonfish'); Wiktionary 'horn, spike, thorn'

kala#1.etymon_note: POLLEX TALA.2, PPN *tala 'narrate'; word kūkala (P&E via POLLEX, PCE *tuu-tara).
kala#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'proclaim, announce'; Wiktionary 'to proclaim, to announce'

kala#2.etymon_note: POLLEX TALA.3, PPN *tala 'untie, undo'; words huikala, kalahala (Andrews: kala 'to loosen; to forgive').
kala#2.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'loosen, untie, free, release'; Wiktionary 'to untie … to absolve, to forgive'

kala#gable.etymon_note: POLLEX files P&E's kala hale under PPN *tara 'the end wall of a house' (TARA), a set apart from the four *tala; Andrews' kala n. 3 agrees. New id for kala hale (was kala?kalahale); it links only through HALE.
kala#gable.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) kala hale 'house gable'; Andrews kala n. 3 'the ends of a house in distinction from the sides'

kanaka.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *taŋata 'person, human being' (TAGATA), Wiktionary's one etymology; words kanaka makua, laukanaka, moʻokanaka, ʻahakanaka.
kanaka.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'man, human, person'; Wiktionary 'man, human, human being'

kani.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *taŋi, TAGI.A 'cry, weep' and TAGI.B 'make a characteristic sound', sub-sets of one set; words kanikau, kaniwāwae, pahu kani and puʻukani all read kani 'sound'.
kani.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'sound' and 'cry out'; Wiktionary 'to sound; cry, peal'

kapu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tapu 'prohibited, under ritual restriction' (TAPU); words pahukapu, ʻai kapu. Wiktionary's kapu#1 'tub' and kapu#2 'cap' are English loans, and no word uses them.
kapu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'taboo, prohibition, sacred, holy, consecrated'; Wiktionary 'taboo, prohibition; something sacred'

kau#1.etymon_note: POLLEX TAU.2, PPN *tau 'hang, be suspended'; words hakakau (perch), kau kānāwai (set a law), kaulike (hang even). Not kau 'season' (*taqu, TAQU.1), the plural particle (TAQU.2A), the numeral-group prefix *tau- (TAU-.14) or 'cover an oven' (TAU.12): see B5.
kau#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'hang, suspend, perch, rest'; Wiktionary 'to place, to put; to perch; to enact; to hang up'

kau#2.etymon_note: Wiktionary gives kau 'chant' its own etymology (PPN *tau 'song'), apart from kau 'place' and kau 'season'; POLLEX has no Hawaiian row for it, so no ancestor is printed. Word kanikau.
kau#2.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'sacred chant; to chant'; Andrews' kanikau bracket 'kau, a song'

kau?kaukahi.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart (B5). POLLEX makes this kau the numeral-group prefix *tau-, not kau 'place' or 'season'; Andrews' bracket 'kau, canoe' has no support. DESIGN §2 makes no prefix a stone, and B5 admits a group-of stone only if P&E glosses it, which no local source shows. Same content as kau?kaulua.
kau?kaukahi.gloss_source: POLLEX: P&E's kaukahi 'standing alone, solitary' is filed under PPN *tau-tasa 'single', from *tau- 'prefix to numerals, deriving nouns which denote a group' (TAU-.14) + *tasa 'one'

kau?kaulua.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart (B5). POLLEX's notes derive *tau-lua from *tau-.14 + *rua; Andrews brackets kau 'place, put' instead, a 19th-century reading F2 does not print. If B5 admits the group-of stone, kau?kaukahi and kau?kaulua become one id and link (single canoe ↔ double canoe).
kau?kaulua.gloss_source: POLLEX: P&E's kaulua 'pair, yoke, two of a kind' (PPN *tau-lua) and 'double canoe' (PCE *tau-rua), both from *tau- (TAU-.14) + *rua 'two'

kau?kaupale.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart: the two sources give different senses and different kau (B5's 'cover an oven' line, or kau 'place'). The card gloss is Andrews' 'partition'; P&E's sense order decides the stone.
kau?kaupale.gloss_source: none settled: P&E via POLLEX files kaupale 'to cover an oven … to keep earth out' under PPN *tau 'cover (an earth oven)' (TAU.12); Andrews reads 'partition, boundary' as kau + pale 'ward off'

kaua.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tau-qa 'war, war-party' (TAU-QA), Wiktionary's one etymology; all eight words (hale kaua … puʻukaua) use 'war'. Not the pronoun kāua 'we two' or Andrews' kaua 'to detain'.
kaua.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'war, battle, army; make war'; Wiktionary 'war, battle; to fight'

kaula.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *taura 'rope' (TAURA); words kaulahao, kaula lei, kaulawaha. Andrews' kaula 'prophet' is P&E kāula (*taaula), another stone.
kaula.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'rope, cord'; Wiktionary 'rope, cord, string'

kaʻa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TAKA.1A, PPN *taka 'revolve, roll, go roundabout'. Wiktionary keeps the cart/vehicle noun in the same etymology, so roll and cart are one stone (B9): kaʻapuni, kaʻahele, olokaʻa, lolokaʻa, kaʻawale, kaʻalalo, kaʻaluna, kaʻakaua, hale kaʻa, kaʻahale. Wiktionary's kaʻa#1 'to pay' is not used. Andrews' 'take effect as a cathartic' is never printed (A8).
kaʻa#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'roll, turn, go past, pass by'; Wiktionary 'to roll, revolve; cart, vehicle'

kaʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX TAKI.1, PPN *taki 'lead, tow, guide'; word alakaʻi (Māori arataki).
kaʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'to lead, direct'; Wiktionary 'to lead'

kea.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tea 'white' (TEA); words kōkea, papakea. Andrews' unmarked kea 'male animal …' is P&E's keʻa, a different spelling and stone (A5).

keiki.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *ta-iti 'young male child' (TA-ITI, from *qiti 'small'); words keiki kāne, keikipapa, pale keiki.
keiki.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'child, offspring, boy, son'; Wiktionary 'child; offspring'

kepa.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tepa 'look sideways, glance at' (TEPA); word poʻokepa (Andrews: kepa 'sideways; edgewise'). Andrews' kepa 'almond tree' (a Bible word) and 'spur' are other words.
kepa.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'look sideways; cut obliquely'; Wiktionary 'to look sideways, to turn to the side'

kia#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TIA.1A, PPN *tia 'a stake, post'; pillar and mast are one set (B9). Pillar: hale kia, kia ahi, kia ao, kiaʻāina, kūkia; mast: kiakahi, kiakolu, kialua. Wiktionary's kia#1 'aim' and kia#2–#3 (English loans 'steer', 'deer') are not used.
kia#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'pillar, prop, post, nail, spike, mast'; Wiktionary 'pillar, post; mast, spar'

kiaʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PEP *tiaki 'to guard; to wait for' (TIAKI); words kiaʻipoʻo, kiaʻipuka, kiaʻipō, luna kiaʻi.
kiaʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'watch, guard'; Wiktionary 'to guard, to watch over'

kiko.etymon_note: POLLEX gives P&E's kiko 'pick up food, as chickens do' under PEP *tito 'peck' (TITO); Wiktionary puts the noun 'dot, point' in the same etymology, so one stone. Words kiko kahi, kikolā, kiko moe, kiko nīnau, kikowaena. The P&E check should confirm 'dot' and 'peck' are one headword.
kiko.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'dot, point, speck; punctuation mark'; Andrews 'a small spot, dot or point'; P&E via POLLEX 'to pick up food (as chickens do)'

kilo.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tiro 'look at' (TIRO); word kiloheʻe (Andrews: kilo 'to look for'). The omen-reading senses in the same P&E entry are not printed.
kilo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'watch closely, examine, observe'; Wiktionary 'to watch, gaze'

kino.etymon_note: POLLEX TINO.A, PPN *tino 'body'; words kinoea, kinopaʻa, kinowai (the states of matter), kino wailua, uhikino.
kino.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'body, person, individual, self; main portion'; Wiktionary 'body; form'

kipa#0.etymon_note: One etymon with kipa 'turn aside' (POLLEX PPN *tipa 'stagger, deviate, turn aside', TIPA): Wiktionary calls 'visit' 'possibly an extension' of it, Andrews has one verb (turn from the path; turn in and lodge), and B9 links them, so Wiktionary's kipa#1 merges here. Word hoakipa.
kipa#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to visit, to call'; Andrews 'to turn in and lodge; to stay with one'; P&E via POLLEX 'turn aside'

kipi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TIPI.1A, PPN *tipi 'cut, slice, slash off'; word kipikua (pickaxe). Wiktionary's kipi#1 'rebel' is another word and not used; POLLEX TIPI.2 (P&E: Hilo name for mound taro patches) is a separate set.
kipi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'dig with sharp tool'; Wiktionary 'to dig with a sharp tool'

kiʻekiʻe.etymon_note: POLLEX TIKE.1B, PEC *tike 'lofty, high, exalted'. POLLEX writes the Hawaiian kiʻe(kiʻe), which is why the batch input showed no POLLEX row. A reduplicated stem as one stone (B7 b), never linked to kiʻe. Word luna kiʻekiʻe.
kiʻekiʻe.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) kiʻe(kiʻe) 'high, lofty, important, exalted'; Wiktionary 'high, lofty'

kiʻi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TIKI.1, PCE *tiki 'carved human image'; words kiʻipalapala, kiʻi pōhaku, kiʻiʻoniʻoni, paʻi kiʻi. Wiktionary's kiʻi#1 'fetch' (PCE *tiki 'fetch') is another set and not used. Andrews' 'idol' is never printed (F1).
kiʻi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'image'; Wiktionary 'a picture, image, drawing, photograph'

koa#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *toa 'a tree (Casuarina)' (TOA). Narrowed to the tree: Wiktionary's koa#0 also holds 'warrior', which POLLEX files under *toqa with 'brave' (koa#1), so luna koa moves there (B8). Word laukoa.

koa#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *toqa 'courageous, warrior' (TOQA), apart from the tree *toa (B8); words makakoa, hoakoa, luna koa.
koa#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'brave, bold, fearless, valiant'; Wiktionary 'warrior; to be brave'

koko.etymon_note: POLLEX TOTO.1, PPN *toto 'blood, sap'; words aʻa koko, omokoko, punikoko, puʻukoko. TOTO.2 (a Euphorbia tree) and Andrews' other koko entries are separate and not used.

kolu.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tolu 'three' (TOLU); word kiakolu. Andrews' kolu 'glue' is an English loan.

komo.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tomo 'enter, penetrate, sink in' (TOMO); words komohale, komoʻāina.
komo.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'enter'; Wiktionary 'to enter, go into'

konakona.etymon_note: No POLLEX set. Wiktionary: reduplication of kona 'wart, bump'; a reduplicated stem as one stone (B7 b), never linked to kona. Word pūkonakona. Andrews' other konakona ('undesirable') is another word.
konakona.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'rough, uneven; muscled, muscular'; Andrews 'strong; not easily tired'

koʻi.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *toki 'adze, axe' (TOKI), which P&E spells koʻi. Andrews' koi n. 'ax; adze' sends the reader to its compounds, and koikahi (a plane) and koilipi (an axe) are tools, so both take this stone, not koi 'urge' (*toi). New id; was koi?koikahi and koi?koilipi.
koʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'adze, axe'; Andrews koi n. 'ax; adze … (see compounds of koi for the specific names)'

kua#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TUQA.1A, PPN *tuqa 'back'; words kualana, kuamauna, kuamoʻo, kuanui, kuapaʻa, kuapuʻu, kuaʻāina, lawakua.
kua#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'back; burden, to carry on the back'; Wiktionary 'back; rear'

kua#1.etymon_note: POLLEX TUA.1, PNP *tua 'fell, chop down', a set apart from *tuqa 'back' (B8); words kipikua, kuapapa (Andrews: kua 'to cut down'). Wiktionary's kua#1 also holds 'windward', which no word here uses and whose etymon is not settled.
kua#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'hew, chop, fell, strike down'; Wiktionary 'to chop, chip, hack'

kua?kuahao.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart (B8): the anvil kua has no POLLEX row, and if P&E keeps it apart from kua 'back', a line to the back words would be false.
kua?kuahao.gloss_source: none settled: Wiktionary reads kua 'back (a place to lay something on)'; Andrews has a separate kua n. 'block on which tapa is beaten; anvil of a blacksmith'

kuene.etymon_note: No POLLEX set and no etymology in Wiktionary. Word kuenehale (Andrews: kuene 'to frame or lay out'). Wiktionary's steward sense is the same entry; Andrews' kuene 'a small quantity; detraction' is another word.
kuene.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to lay out, to put in order'; Andrews 'to frame; to lay out, as the frame of a building'

kuhi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX TUSU.A, PPN *tusu 'point (to), indicate'; TUSU.B lists P&E's lima kuhi 'index finger' itself (Sāmoan lima tusi). Word lima kuhi.
kuhi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) 'point'; Wiktionary 'to point at; gesture'

kuhi#1.etymon_note: No etymology in Wiktionary and no POLLEX row; kept apart from kuhi 'point', as Wiktionary and Andrews keep it. Word kuhihewa (Andrews: kuhi 'infer' + hewa 'wrong').
kuhi#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to surmise, to infer; to suppose'; Andrews 'to infer; to surmise'

kui?kuilua.etymon_note: Unresolved, kept apart: the first root may be kui 'string, join' (PPN *tui) or kuʻi 'join, splice', and Andrews writes no ʻokina, so even the stone's spelling waits on P&E.

kulaʻi.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'push over, overthrow'; Wiktionary 'to push over'

kuli#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tuli 'deaf', a set apart from *turi 'knee'; word kulihiamoe.

kuli#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *turi 'knee', a set apart from *tuli 'deaf'; word hāliʻikuli (Andrews bracket 'kuli, knee').

kumu.etymon_note: POLLEX PEP *tumu: TUMU.1A 'origin, base' and 1B 'teacher' are sub-senses of one set, so one stone (B8/B9); words kumu alakaʻi (teacher), kumukānāwai, kumukūʻai (Andrews' 'price' sense), kumulau, kumupaʻa, kumuwai.

kupuna.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tupuna 'grandparent, ancestor'; words kupuna wahine, moʻokupuna.

kuʻi#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tuki 'pound, hammer, strike'; words kuʻihao, kuʻi ʻai.
kuʻi#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'pound, punch, strike'; Wiktionary 'to pound, to strike'

kuʻi#1.etymon_note: Wiktionary's separate kuʻi 'join, unite, stitch'; no etymology and no POLLEX row, so no ancestor; kept apart from kuʻi 'pound' (*tuki) so kuʻikahi does not link to kuʻihao or kuʻi ʻai.
kuʻi#1.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to join, to unite; to stitch'; Andrews 'to stick together; to join'

kāhili.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *taafiri 'to fan, sweep' (P&E kāhili 'to brush, sweep; a ceremonial standard'); one stone though reanalysable as kā + hili; word paʻa kāhili.
kāhili.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'a ceremonial standard'; Wiktionary 'feather standard mounted on a pole'

kālai.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *talai 'hew, carve'; Andrews' 'divide out; manage' senses are in the same entry; words kālai pōhaku, kālaiʻāina.

kāmaʻa.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'sandals or other footwear'; Wiktionary 'sandal, slipper; shoe'

kāne.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *taqane 'male', not PCE *taane (a lunar night name); the common noun only, never the god's name; words keiki kāne, kāne make, makua kāne.
kāne.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'male, husband, man'; Wiktionary 'male; man; husband'

kānāwai.etymon_note: No POLLEX row and no inherited etymon in the sources; Wiktionary's kā + nā + wai is a folk etymology, so the whole word is one stone; words kau kānāwai, kumukānāwai, luna kānāwai.
kānāwai.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'code, law, statute'; Andrews 'to put under the law'

kāwili.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *taa-wili 'rotate, spin, whirl' (< *wili 'twist'), filed under P&E kāwili 'to mix'; Andrews gives the bird-lime sense as sense 2 of the same verb; word kāwilimanu.
kāwili.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to snare'; Andrews 'to ensnare birds with bird lime' (v. 2)

kē.etymon_note: POLLEX PEC *tee 'negative' (TEE.2*, P&E kē 'protest, oppose, refuse'), not PCE *tee 'emit a sharp sound'; word kēʻai.
kē.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'protest, complaint; to oppose, refuse'; Wiktionary 'to protest'

kī#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tii, the ti plant; not kī 'shoot, squirt' or the loans kī 'key', kī 'tea'; word lau kī.

kō#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PEP *too 'sugarcane', not PNP *too 'conceive', PCE *too 'your' or PPN *toho 'drag'; words hākō, kōkea, kōpaʻa, kōʻula, lau kō, monakō.

kōhi#0.etymon_note: Wiktionary kōhi 1 'split off with a blade' (Wiktionary gives PPN *tofi, but POLLEX has no Hawaiian row, so none printed); Andrews' 'to dig' fits it, not kōhi 2 'gather'; word kōhiʻai.
kōhi#0.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to break or split something off with a blade, such as a shovel'; Andrews bracket 'kohi, to dig'

kū#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tuqu 'stand' (TUQU.1); kept only where a source gives 'stand' for the word (B4): helekū, iwikū, kūemi, kūkaha, kūkala, kūkia, kūlehu, kūlālā, kūnihi, kūnānā, kūola, kūpaʻa, kūpono, kūpuni, kūʻai, kūʻē, kūʻēʻē, pākū.
kū#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'stand, upright, to be'; Wiktionary 'to stand, to rise; to stop'

kū?kūhewa.etymon_note: Unresolved (B4): Andrews reads kū 'to be hit'; POLLEX has a separate kū 'abruptly, rudely' < PPN *tuqu 'cut' (flagged uncertain) that may be this one; P&E decides.

kū?kūloko.etymon_note: Unresolved (B4): Andrews reads kū 'pertaining to', his adjective kū 'belonging to; befitting', not 'stand'; P&E decides.
kū?kūloko.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket 'ku, pertaining to'; Andrews adj. kū 'belonging to' (placeholder)

kū?kūmaka.etymon_note: Unresolved (B4): Andrews reads kū 'to be hit' (his kū v. 7); no source says it is kū 'stand'; P&E decides.

kū?kūʻau.etymon_note: Unresolved (B4): POLLEX files kūʻau 'handle, stem' under PPN *tuu-kau 'handle, haft', whose *tuu- is not *tuqu 'stand' and is unglossed; no gloss printed.
kū?kūʻau.gloss_source: none: no source glosses kū in kūʻau

kū?kūʻauhau.etymon_note: Unresolved (B4): POLLEX segments Kuu/ʔauhau/ and leaves kū unglossed; Andrews' 'kū = kuamoʻo, path' is a 19th-century guess; may be a kū- formative; no gloss printed.
kū?kūʻauhau.gloss_source: none: Andrews' 'short for kuamoʻo, path' is a guess

kūkulu#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *tulu-tulu 'house post'; P&E (via POLLEX) glosses one item 'pillar, post; to build', so kūkulu#1 'build' is merged in; 'horizon, compass point' is the same word in Andrews and Wiktionary; words kūkulu hema, kūkulupapa.
kūkulu#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'pillar, post; to build a house'; Wiktionary 'pillar, post; horizon, compass point'

kūlou.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *tuulou 'to bow, deference'; one stone, not Andrews' kū + lou; word kūloupoʻo.
kūlou.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'to bow the head, bend'; Wiktionary 'to bow'

kūʻai.etymon_note: No POLLEX row; Wiktionary's kū + ʻai is uncited and may be folk etymology; as a stone it is the whole word; word kumukūʻai.
kūʻai.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'to barter'; Andrews 'to barter; to traffic'

kūʻauhau.etymon_note: POLLEX files kūʻauhau 'genealogist' under PCE *kaufau 'an ordered list or recitation' (the ʻauhau part); word moʻokūʻauhau.

lae#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *laqe: forehead (LAQE.A) and promontory (LAQE.B) are sub-senses of one set, so Wiktionary's lae#1 'headland' is merged in; word laelua.
lae#0.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'forehead' and 'promontory'; Andrews 'a brow of a hill; a cape or headland'

lahi.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *lafi 'thin'; word maʻalahi (no source explains how maʻa + lahi give 'easy').

lalo.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *lalo 'below, under' (LALO.A; LALO.B 'south' is a sub-sense of the same set); words kaʻalalo, papalalo.

lama#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *rama 'torch'; not lama 'ebony' (PNP *lama) or lama 'rum' (a loan); word laulama.

lana#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PNP *laŋa 'be afloat'; Wiktionary's lana#0 also holds 'aware of sounds on waking' (PPN *ŋana), which no word uses; words halelana, kualana, lanaau, manaʻolana, wailana.

lani.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *laŋi 'sky' (LAGI.2); Andrews reads lani 'heaven, on high' in all four words, so POLLEX's separate LAGI.5 'chiefly rank' set is not attached; words hiʻilani, hūlani, lewa lani, pōʻailani.

lau#0.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *lau 'leaf' (LAU.1A); words kumulau, lau hala, lauhoe, laukoa, lau kī, lau kō, laumake, lauwili, lau ʻulu.

lau#1.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *lau 'indefinite large number' (LAU.2B); POLLEX also files the Hawaiian under *rau 'hundred'; words laukanaka, laulama, laulima.
lau#1.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'many, numerous, four hundred'; Wiktionary 'many, numerous'

lau#broad.etymon_note: New: POLLEX files laupapa and laulā under PPN *lau 'expanse, breadth' (LAU.3), and laupapa itself as PPN *lau-papa 'broad flat surface'; not lau 'leaf'; word laupapa.
lau#broad.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) laupapa 'broad, flat (of coral, lava, reef)', laulā 'broad, wide'; set LAU.3 'surface area, expanse, breadth'

lawa#bind.etymon_note: New: POLLEX PPN *lawa 'bind, wrap' (LAWA.2), apart from lawa 'enough' (LAWA.1A); Andrews' bracket 'lawa, to bind'; word lawakua.
lawa#bind.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'bind'; Andrews 'to hold fast; to bind tightly'

lawaiʻa.etymon_note: POLLEX PCE *rawa-ika 'to fish; fisherman' (historically lawe + iʻa), one stone; words hoalawaiʻa, lawaiʻa manu.
lawaiʻa.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'fisherman; to fish'; Wiktionary 'fisherman; to fish'

lawe.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *lawe 'take, lay hold of'; words lawehala, lawehana, laweola.
lawe.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'take, accept, carry, bring'; Wiktionary 'to carry, take'

laʻa#season.etymon_note: New, provisional: Andrews' laʻa n. 'season', which both definitions use ('time when vegetables die / grow fast'); not laʻa 'sacred' (PPN *laka), though Andrews' brackets say 'devoted'; words laʻamake, laʻaulu.
laʻa#season.gloss_source: Andrews–Parker 1922 laʻa n. 'time of; season' (placeholder until P&E)

lehu.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *refu 'ashes'; words kūlehu, lehu ahi.

lei.etymon_note: POLLEX files Hawaiian lei (P&E 'ivory necklace') under PPN *lei 'whale tooth, ivory', the neck ornament; not PNP *lei 'leap'; words kaula lei, lei aliʻi, lei hala.
lei.gloss_source: Wiktionary 'a wreath of flowers or leaves; necklace'; Andrews 'necklace; wreath; garland'

lele.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *lele 'fly, run, leap'; words aʻalele, hikilele, hōkūlele, lelehuna, lelepono, mokulele, moʻo lele, wailele, ʻukulele.
lele.gloss_source: POLLEX (P&E) 'fly, jump, run'; Wiktionary 'to jump, leap; to fly'

leo.etymon_note: POLLEX PPN *leqo 'voice'; words leopaʻa, leowaena, leo wahine, pāleo.

leoleo.etymon_note: Reduplication of leo (Wiktionary); no POLLEX row; its own stone, never linked to LEO (B7); word pāleoleo.

ʻau#group.etymon_note: POLLEX KAU.2B PPN *kau "group of people, company", which P&E cites with ʻau waʻa itself. Word auwaʻa (form ʻauwaʻa). Same set as ʻaumoana (POLLEX >> CE *kau-moana); id to be shared with the ʻau batch.
ʻau#group.gloss_source: POLLEX (Pukui & Elbert 1986) "Group (in ʻau waʻa, ʻau moku)"; Andrews–Parker 1922 bracket "au, a number"

alahaka.reason: POLLEX (P&E) alahaka "plank bridge, ladder" < PCE *ara-fata "bridge or ladder", cf. PPN *fata "shelf": haka "shelf, platform" (haka#0), not haka "gap".

aumoe.reason: POLLEX (P&E) and Wiktionary derive aumoe from *aqu-mohe "fast asleep", not *qau "current"; Andrews reads au "time". Split off the current stone, left unresolved.

auwaʻa.reason: Form ʻauwaʻa; POLLEX (P&E) glosses ʻau "group (in ʻau waʻa)" < PPN *kau "group of people". Not au "current".

hauʻoli.reason: POLLEX (P&E) lists hau/ʻoli under PPN *sau "(in compounds) temperament"; Wiktionary agrees. Not hau "dew" or "hibiscus".

holoʻai.reason: Resolved: Andrews brackets holo 'bundle' and POLLEX (P&E) has holo 'a long bundle, as of hard poi' (PNP *solo, SOLO.2B), a set apart from holo 'run'.

huamele.reason: Resolved: Andrews brackets hua 'letter' and POLLEX (P&E) has hua 'word, letter, figure' apart from *fua 'fruit'; the two agree, so hua?huamele becomes hua#word (A2).

huaʻōlelo.reason: Split of the old hua id: the word means 'word' and P&E's hua 'word, letter' (POLLEX, apart from *fua) is the root A2 assigns it. Wiktionary reads hua 'seed, fruit' and the adjudicator had left it unresolved; the P&E check should confirm.

kahawai.reason: Withdrawn from kaha#1: Wiktionary reads kaha 'place', Andrews 'cut'; the adjudication and P18 say a sense id only when sources agree, so the link to kahakai and kahaone waits for P&E's Lit.

kahuahi.reason: Resolved: POLLEX puts kahu 'keeper' and kahu 'tend an oven' in one set (PPN *tafu, TAFU.A–C, and PMQ *tafu(-afi), Marquesan tahuahi 'servant who lights the fire'), so either reading is the same root as kahu akua and kahu ʻāina.

kalahale.reason: Resolved: POLLEX (P&E) kala hale 'house gable' < PPN *tara 'end wall of a house', and Andrews' kala n. 3 'the ends of a house'; a fifth kala, apart from the *tala sets.

koikahi.reason: Resolved: Andrews' koi n. 'ax; adze' sends the reader to its compounds; the tool word takes koʻi 'adze' (P&E spelling, PPN *toki), as the form koʻikahi already does.

koilipi.reason: Resolved: koʻi 'adze, axe' (PPN *toki) + lipi 'sharp edge' for an axe; Andrews' koi n. 'ax; adze' points to this compound. Form koʻilipi.

kūkulupapa.reason: kūkulu#1 merged into kūkulu#0: POLLEX (P&E) glosses one kūkulu 'pillar, post; to build a house' (PNP *tulu-tulu).

laelua.reason: lae#1 merged into lae#0: POLLEX forehead (LAQE.A) and promontory (LAQE.B) are one set, PPN *laqe.

laupapa.reason: Resolves lau?laupapa: POLLEX (P&E) files laupapa under PPN *lau 'expanse, breadth' and as PPN *lau-papa 'broad flat surface', not lau 'leaf'.

lawakua.reason: Resolves lawa?lawakua: Andrews' bracket 'lawa, to bind' is POLLEX/P&E lawa 'bind' (PPN *lawa, LAWA.2), not lawa 'enough'.

laʻamake.reason: Resolves laʻa?laʻamake: Andrews defines it 'time when vegetables die', his laʻa n. 'season'; shares the stone with laʻaulu (provisional until P&E).

laʻaulu.reason: Resolves laʻa?laʻaulu: Andrews defines it 'time when vegetables grow fast', his laʻa n. 'season'; shares the stone with laʻamake (provisional until P&E).

lunakoa.reason: Split of koa#0: 'soldier' (Andrews' bracket) belongs with brave/warrior under PPN *toqa (POLLEX), not with the koa tree (*toa).
